purpose: Separate public playback starts, owner-only engagement, replaying retention segments, and unobserved video completion and cross-video session durations.

metrics.label: Public watch-page views
metrics.limit: Playback-start event count; not unique people or whole-video completions

metrics.label: Estimated unique viewers
metrics.limit: Estimated distinct viewers in selected window; not a number of completed videos

metrics.label: Impressions click-through rate
metrics.limit: Selection after eligible shown thumbnail, not viewer retention after click

metrics.label: Shorts stayed to watch
metrics.limit: Stayed past initial seconds rather than swiped away; not full Short completion

metrics.label: Shorts engaged views
metrics.limit: View events passing initial watch threshold, excluding loops; not completion

metrics.label: Average view duration
metrics.limit: Average viewed minutes among engaged events; not an entire viewing session across videos

metrics.label: Average percentage viewed
metrics.limit: Average percent among engaged watch events, not the fraction of people who reached end

metrics.label: Intro at 30 seconds
metrics.limit: Only owner video-level report; relative survival to 30 seconds, not completion

metrics.label: Segment replay or abandonment
metrics.limit: May exceed overall video view count because of rewatches, not number of unique people

metrics.label: Watch time hours
metrics.limit: Aggregate hours are not a unique viewer count, completion count, or net revenue

metrics.label: Time in cross-video YouTube session
metrics.limit: General total YouTube multi-video session duration is not disclosed by these reports

unit_comparison_gates: Require owner authorization to access retention curves; never infer private engagement metrics from public counts.
Record metric definition, format, video duration, observation window and the August 2026 counting epoch.
Shorts stayed-to-watch is initial threshold retention; it does not provide full end-card completion.
Average percentage viewed is an average across engaged watch events, not a binary count of completed people.
Watch-time totals and average view duration do not identify a visitor's total session across videos.
Replay spikes and repeat segment views may exceed the number of video view events; a spike is not an audience growth rate.
Different formats and length cohorts need comparable definitions; missing values are null, not zero.
